affectedPublicSurfaces: THE CREDENTIAL ROW — WHICH ALREADY CARRIES SCOPES. The issue's premise, 'No scope is stored anywhere', is FALSE and the executor must not act on it. `models.py::TikTokCredential.scopes` is `Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)`, created by migration `001_create_users_shops_tiktok_credentials.py` at the very start of the project; `repositories/tiktok_credentials.py` already accepts and writes `scopes: str | None`; and `core/security/tiktok_oauth.py` already extracts them from the token response — `token_data.get("scopes")`, falling back to `granted_scopes` and comma-joining a list. THERE IS NO MIGRATION TO WRITE HERE. The issue's note that 'the scope column is an additive migration reserved through Meta' describes work that was done years ago.

THE REAL DEFECT, which is narrower and sharper than the issue states: scopes are written ONLY on the `cred_repo.create(...)` branch — a BRAND-NEW credential. On the `cred_repo.update_tokens(...)` branch, taken when `get_by_merchant` finds an EXISTING credential, `scopes` is NOT passed at all, so the stored list is never refreshed. That is precisely the owner's 2026-09-07 note ('the connected shops must re-authorise once for newly enabled scopes to appear') colliding with the code: a re-authorisation by an already-connected shop takes the update branch and leaves the scope list STALE. Fixing that branch is the substance of this slice.

A NEW CAPABILITY CHECK ON THE VENDOR BOUNDARY. `has_scope(shop, scope)` becomes readable per shop, and every resource method that requires a scope DECLARES it and refuses with a named `ScopeMissing` BEFORE any HTTP call — a fail-closed guard at the boundary (S-NFR-1). The workflow maps that refusal to `scope_unavailable`, a cause #1707 added. Nothing about the transport, signing or retry behaviour changes.

SECOND CONTRADICTION — THE NAMED FILES DO NOT HOLD WHAT THE ISSUE SAYS. `integrations/tiktok/auth.py` is `TikTokAuth`: token exchange and refresh only (`exchange_code`, `refresh_access_token`). It is NOT the callback and it persists nothing. The callback is `api/routes/auth_tiktok.py::tiktok_oauth_callback` → `services/tiktok/oauth.py::complete_tiktok_oauth_callback` → `core/security/tiktok_oauth.py`. And `integrations/tiktok/resources/products.py` has NO diagnosis method at all — its methods are `search`, `search_all`, `get_details`, `create`, `edit`, `get_categories`, `check_listing_prerequisites`, `get_category_attributes`, `get_brands`, `get_seo_words`, `get_suggestions`, `upload_product_image`, `upload_product_file`, `update_prices`. Acceptance criterion 2 names a method that does not exist; assert the guard on a REAL scoped method (or on a declared-scope method added deliberately and named in the PR), never on a stub written to satisfy the criterion.

NO HTTP SURFACE CHANGES: the OAuth callback route keeps its path, its redirect and its status codes; no /v1 route is added or altered; no response model gains a field. Scopes are runtime knowledge, not seller-facing data — do NOT expose them on any route in this slice.

The OAuth callback is exercised through the REAL `complete_tiktok_oauth_callback` with the token response bound to a fake built on the real vendor payload shape, never a `**kwargs` double, and the scope refusal is asserted on a RECORDING TRANSPORT so 'no HTTP call was made' is a fact about the wire rather than an inference from a branch. Post-deploy: ONE re-authorisation on the candidate against the sandbox shop, then read the credential row back; no public traffic reaches a candidate task set and no production write occurs.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE IN THIS SLICE, and the issue's note to the contrary is wrong. `tiktok_credentials.scopes` (Text, nullable) ALREADY EXISTS — created by migration `001_create_users_shops_tiktok_credentials.py` and declared on `models.py::TikTokCredential` — and `repositories/tiktok_credentials.py` already writes it on the create path. Do NOT reserve or write a migration number, do NOT add a second scope column, and do NOT change the column's type or nullability: NULL is a meaningful value here ('this credential predates the fix, and we do not know what was granted') and defaulting it to an empty list would be a claim the data does not support. Old and new code coexist because the schema is identical before and after; only which branch writes the column changes.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Scopes keep being written only when a credential is first created and never on re-authorisation, so a shop that re-authorises for newly enabled scopes still shows the old list; nothing checks a scope before a call, and a missing scope keeps failing at the vendor or not at all. That is the pre-existing state — including the stale-on-update branch, which stays broken rather than half-fixed.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. There is NO schema to revert and NO downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration, and the `scopes` column predates it by the entire life of the project. Scope lists already persisted stay VALID and simply stop being consulted: the previous code neither reads them nor refuses on them, so every call reverts to the pre-existing behaviour of failing at the vendor instead of at the boundary. Nothing is stranded, no credential is invalidated, and no re-authorisation is undone. The honest caveat to state in the PR: the previous release will keep the scope list stale on re-authorisation again, so any operator instruction to 'have the shops re-authorise' becomes ineffective the moment the rollback lands. If #1701's, #1706's, #1707's, #1709's or #1712's schema is being reverted in the same operation, those downgrades are theirs and must FAIL LOUDLY on any non-product `subject_type` row, NULL `product_id`, `waiting_external` row, new stop-reason cause, non-default confirmation `kind`, or any act-record row.

doNotInfer: Do NOT read a migration number from head, and do NOT write a migration at all. `tiktok_credentials.scopes` already exists (migration `001_create_users_shops_tiktok_credentials.py`, `models.py::TikTokCredential.scopes`); the issue's note reserving a number is wrong. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.
Do NOT add a second scope column, a scopes table, or a JSON re-encoding of what is already a Text column. One place, already chosen.

Do NOT blank the scope list when the vendor returns no scope field. An absent field means the vendor said nothing, never that the shop granted nothing; clearing the column would turn a silent omission into a fleet-wide capability outage the next time anything checks.

Do NOT treat NULL as 'no scopes granted' without deciding. Every credential written before this fix has NULL. State the policy in the PR — proceed-and-let-the-vendor-answer, or refuse — and assert it; an unstated NULL policy either breaks every existing shop or makes the guard useless on all of them.

Do NOT write a diagnosis method to satisfy acceptance criterion 2. `integrations/tiktok/resources/products.py` has no such method; assert the guard on a real scoped method and name it, rather than adding a stub whose only caller is a test.

Do NOT edit `integrations/tiktok/auth.py` expecting to find the callback. `TikTokAuth` does token exchange and refresh only; the persistence path is `api/routes/auth_tiktok.py::tiktok_oauth_callback` → `services/tiktok/oauth.py` → `core/security/tiktok_oauth.py`, and the branch that needs fixing is the `update_tokens(...)` one.

Do NOT make the HTTP call and then check. The refusal happens BEFORE the transport — a fail-closed guard at the boundary (S-NFR-1) — and 'no call was made' must be asserted on a recording transport, not on a code branch.
Do NOT invent a new stop reason. `scope_unavailable` is #1707's and the vocabulary is closed; a cause coined at the call site would fail the CHECK constraint anyway.

Do NOT expose scopes on any /v1 route or in any seller-facing string. They are runtime knowledge, not seller data, and a scope name is exactly the kind of internal identifier the outbound guard forbids (S-NFR-4).
Do NOT log a token, a refresh token or a `shop_cipher` while touching this path, and do NOT weaken the #1200 credential-binding verification that runs before any write.

Do NOT derive the subject from revenue, do NOT emit a per-order card, do NOT reuse the emission-budget suppression vocabulary (`active_cap`/`cooldown`/`weekly_novelty_cap`), do NOT add a second reaper policy object, and do NOT add a push, email or Zalo transport — none of it belongs in a credential slice.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/** — this epic's doNotLoad list.

Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature — the real callback path, the real credentials repository, the real resource method and a recording transport built on the real client's interface. A `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real call would work.
